extracted.intended_audience: public relations counsel, business executives, and political campaign strategists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for designing and executing public-relations/propaganda campaigns for business and political purposes, including audience research, messaging, crisis handling, and campaign budgeting/planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common_denominator_of_interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The application of a principle of a common denominator of interest between the object that is sold and the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by a shoe manufacturer organizing a 'foot protection bureau' to disseminate scientifically accurate information on proper foot care, thereby furthering both public welfare and product sales. Use programs that simultaneously serve the public and promote the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create_and_maintain_sympathetic_public_opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: "It matters not... if you haven't behind you a sympathetic public opinion, you are bound to fail." — public opinion and good will are essential to business expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public acceptance facilitates mergers, stock/bond issues, and general expansion. Deliberate effort to build good will is necessary and must be continuously maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate_use_of_propaganda_as_business_tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The growth of mammoth enterprises has, to a great extent, been obtained by a deliberate use of propaganda in its broadest sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propaganda may modify public opinion and the business concern itself (e.g., free testing labs, cookery schools). Use varied channels and collaborations to shape perceptions and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate_and_avert_negative_public_trends
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel should anticipate such trends of public opinion and advise on how to avert them, either by convincing the public that its fears or prejudices are unjustified, or in certain cases by modifying the action of the client to the extent necessary to remove the cause of complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey public opinion to discover irreducible opposition, distinguish logical explanations from habitual emotional reactions and clichés, and recommend persuasion or policy modification accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency_and_information_disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Some corporations refuse to give out sufficient information to permit the public to know the true condition of the concern; lack of such disclosure undermines public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate financial and operational information to prevent misunderstandings and suspicions. Particularly important for semi-public utilities which face demands for public or municipal ownership if contact with the public is not maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public_relations_for_financial_operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of stock and bond issues depends upon the general record of the concern in the business world, and also upon the good will which it has been able to create in the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate public recognition and acceptance before attempting large financings or mergers; public opinion can determine the success of major financial operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_PR_to_counteract_unethical_or_exaggerated_advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: The new technique of public relations counsel is serving a very useful purpose in business by... helping to break down unfair competitive exaggerated and overemphatic advertising by reaching the public with the truth through other channels than advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ channels such as clinics, clubs, professional bodies, the trade press, and daily press to educate the public about authentic product capabilities (example: toothpaste manufacturers using dental clinics, women's clubs, medical colleges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate_beyond_price_through_style_and_perception
rubrics_metrics.description: The logical way out of cut-throat price competition is for the manufacturer to develop some sales appeal other than mere cheapness, to give the product, in the public mind, some other attraction, some idea that will modify the product slightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use principles familiar to the propagandist—gregariousness, obedience to authority, emulation—to establish minor elements (color, style) as matters of fashion or identity so mass products can be split up in public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate_authority_endorsements_and_influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: It was found that four groups might help to change hat fashions: the society leader, the style expert, the fashion editor and writer, the artist ... A committee of prominent artists was organized ... A committee was formed of distinguished American women ... A style committee was formed of editors of fashion magazines and other prominent fashion authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble and use influential groups (artists, style committees, editors, prominent citizens, mannequins) and staged events to create trends and drive consumer behavior (millinery example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis_management_and_countering_false_rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: Often the public relations counsel is called in to handle an emergency situation. A false rumor, for instance, may occasion an enormous loss in prestige and money if not handled promptly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly and strategically; sometimes public gestures or community recognition (Beech‑Nut 'home town' event) are more convincing than simple denials. Technical handling of public relations in emergencies can prevent large financial loss (Hudson Motor rumor example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism_and_avoidance_of_stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: The modern publicity director ... is a business man, responsible for the security of tens or hundreds of millions of dollars ... He cannot afford to be a stunt artist or a free‑lance adventurer in publicity. He must know his public accurately and modify its thoughts and actions by means of the methods which the amusement world has learned from its old pupil, big business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice disciplined, research‑based public relations rather than sensational stunts; match tactics to improving public taste and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous_public_study_and_pulse-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern business must have its finger continuously on the public pulse. It must understand the changes in the public mind and be prepared to interpret itself fairly and eloquently to changing opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ongoing market/public opinion research and adapt messaging and policies to shifts in tastes and attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_business_methods_in_political_campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The politician understands the public... But the politician is not necessarily a general sales manager, a public relations counsel, or a man who knows how to secure mass distribution of ideas. Big business ... prepares its policies carefully and in selling an idea to the large buying public of America, it must proceed according to broad plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political campaigns should adopt business practices: market analysis, planned mass distribution of ideas, budgeting, and professional public relations to reach large electorates rather than rely on antiquated side‑shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine_objectives_and_express_them_as_honest_platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step in a political campaign is to determine the objectives, and to express them exceedingly well in the current form—that is, as a platform. In devising the platform the leader should be sure that it is an honest platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform planks and pledges should be clear, credible and treated with guarantee‑like seriousness; the public has lost faith in campaign promises, so honesty and durable commitments build trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific_analysis_of_public_and_targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid in the preparation of the platform there should be made as nearly scientific an analysis as possible of the public and of the needs of the public. A survey of public desires and demands would come to the aid of the political strategist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys and market segmentation to avoid wasting resources on irrecoverable segments and to inform product/policy changes and message presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget_and_plan_propaganda_expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: As in the business field, the expenses of the political campaign should be budgeted. A large business to‑day knows exactly how much money it is going to spend on propaganda during the next year or years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate specific percentages to different channels (newspaper, magazine, outdoor, circularization, sales promotion, travel). Treat campaign expenditure with the same forecasting and apportionment as corporate advertising budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design_campaigns_for_mass_distribution_and_repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: A company makes out its sales budget for the year, it subdivides the circulations of the various magazines and newspapers it uses in advertising and calculates with a fair degree of accuracy how many times a section of that population is subjected to the appeal... It knows approximately to what extent a national campaign duplicates and repeats the emphasis of a local campaign of selling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan media selection and frequency systematically to achieve desired exposure and avoid counterproductive duplication; apply same methods to political messaging to maximize reach and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify_client_action_when_necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel should ... advise some action or modification of policy calculated to make the readjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public objection is grounded in real causes, counsel should recommend actual policy or operational changes in the client organization rather than solely attempting persuasion.
